label: thm:continuum-well-posedness
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Continuum well-posedness and dead core

title: Proof
body_md:
Existence, uniqueness, regularity, and
\eqref{eq:continuum-dead-core-measure} follow from
\cite{CaffarelliFarahRestrepo2025}. For $x\in D_u$, the superlevel set
at $u(x)$ is $D_u$, giving
\eqref{eq:superlevel-measure-on-dead-core}. If $x\notin D_u$, then
$u(x)<\max_{\overline\Omega}u$; by continuity,
$\{u>u(x)\}$ contains a neighbourhood of $D_u$ and hence has measure
strictly greater than $\alpha$. This proves
\eqref{eq:superlevel-measure-off-dead-core}.

label: lem:mass-lumping-error
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Mass-lumping error

title: Proof
body_md:
On $K\in\ensuremath{\varTheta}\xspace$, the local quadrature error is $\int_K \bigl(
I_K(p_hr_h)-p_hr_h \bigr) \,\mathrm dx,$ where
\[
  I_K(p_hr_h)(x)-p_h(x)r_h(x) = \sum_{j=1}^3 \lambda_j(x)p_h(x_j)
  \bigl( r_h(x_j)-r_h(x) \bigr).
\]
Since $r_h$ is affine, $\ensuremath{\left|r_h(x_j)-r_h(x)\right|}\leq
Ch_K\ensuremath{\left|\nabla r_h|_K\right|}.$
Thus
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|
    \int_K
    \bigl(
      I_K(p_hr_h)-p_hr_h
    \bigr)
    \,\mathrm dx
  \right|}
  \leq
  Ch_K
  \ensuremath{\left\|p_h\right\|}_{L^\infty(K)}
  \ensuremath{\left|K\right|}
  \ensuremath{\left|\nabla r_h|_K\right|}.
\]
Summation and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\eqref{eq:mass-lumping-error}.

title: Proof
body_md:
In interior nodal coordinates, the hypothesis is $A_hV\leq A_hW$.
Since $A_h^{-1}$ is entrywise nonnegative, $V-W = A_h^{-1}(A_hV-A_hW)
\leq0.$

label: lem:discrete-rearrangement-concavity
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Concavity and continuity of $\mathcal R_h$

title: Proof
body_md:
The representation
\eqref{eq:discrete-minimum-representation} expresses $\mathcal R_h$ as
the pointwise minimum of linear functionals, so it is concave. If
$(E_i)$ minimises the representation at $w_h$, then
\[
  \mathcal R_h(v_h)-\mathcal R_h(w_h)
  \leq
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_i
  \bigl(
    v_h(x_i)-w_h(x_i)
  \bigr),
\]
where $0\leq q_i\leq M_\alpha$. Interchanging $v_h$ and $w_h$ proves
\eqref{eq:discrete-rearrangement-Lipschitz}.
head: environment

label: lem:canonical-source-supergradient
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:canonical-source-supergradient}
Let $c\in\mathcal L_h(v_h)$ and set
\[
  I_c
  :=
  \mathcal I_h(c;v_h),
  \qquad
  \omega_c
  :=
  \ensuremath{\left|I_c\right|}.
  \]
  There is a partition of $I_c$ among the nodes satisfying
$v_h(x_i)=c$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \frac{1}{\omega_i}
  \int_{E_i}G(\rho) \ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\rho
  =
  \frac{1}{\omega_c}
  \int_{I_c}G(\rho) \ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\rho.
  \label{eq:equal-average-allocation}
\end{equation}
Consequently, the canonical source
$\overline q_h[v_h]$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R_h(w_h)-\mathcal R_h(v_h)
  \leq
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_i
  \overline q_{h,i}[v_h]
  \bigl(
    w_h(x_i)-v_h(x_i)
  \bigr)
  \label{eq:canonical-source-supergradient}
\end{equation}
for every $w_h\inV_h$.
head: environment
name: Canonical tied-level source

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
  \mathcal N_c
  :=
  \ensuremath{\left\{{
    i\in\mathcal N_h:
    v_h(x_i)=c
  }\right\}}
  =
  \ensuremath{\left\{{
    i_1,\ldots,i_m
  }\right\}}.
\]
On $I_c$, define the vector measure
\[
  \nu(E)
  :=
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    \ensuremath{\left|E\right|},
    \int_E G(\rho)\ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\rho
  }\right)},
  \qquad
  E\subset I_c
  \text{ measurable}.
\]
Since Lebesgue measure is nonatomic and $G\in L^\infty(I_c)$, the
vector measure $\nu$ is nonatomic. Hence, by the Lyapunov convexity
theorem, the range of the restriction of $\nu$ to any measurable
subset $A\subset I_c$ is convex. In particular, for every
$\lambda\in[0,1]$ there exists a measurable set $E\subset A$ such that
$\nu(E) = \lambda\nu(A).$

We now construct the required partition recursively. Set $A_1:=I_c$
and $W_k:=\sum_{\ell=k}^m\omega_{i_\ell}$. Since $W_1=\omega_c$, we
have $\nu(A_1)=\nu(I_c)=\frac{W_1}{\omega_c}\nu(I_c)$. Suppose that a
measurable remainder $A_k$ has been constructed with
$\nu(A_k)=\frac{W_k}{\omega_c}\nu(I_c)$.
By the preceding convexity property, there exists
$E_{i_k}\subset A_k$ such that
$\nu(E_{i_k})=\frac{\omega_{i_k}}{W_k}\nu(A_k)=
\frac{\omega_{i_k}}{\omega_c}\nu(I_c)$.
Set $A_{k+1} := A_k\setminus E_{i_k}.$ Then $\nu(A_{k+1}) =
\frac{W_{k+1}}{\omega_c}\nu(I_c),$ so the construction may be
continued. Taking the final remainder as $E_{i_m}$ gives a measurable
partition of $I_c$ satisfying
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|E_i\right|}
  =
  \omega_i,
  \qquad
  \int_{E_i}G(\rho)\ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\rho
  =
  \frac{\omega_i}{\omega_c}
  \int_{I_c}G(\rho)\ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\rho.
\]
Dividing the second identity by $\omega_i$ proves
\eqref{eq:equal-average-allocation}.

Applying this construction independently on every tied nodal level
gives a minimising rank allocation for which $\mathcal R_h(v_h) =
\sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h} \omega_i \overline q_{h,i}[v_h]v_h(x_i).$ Using the
same allocation as a competitor in the minimum representation of
$\mathcal R_h(w_h)$ yields
\[
  \mathcal R_h(w_h)-\mathcal R_h(v_h)
  \leq
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_i
  \overline q_{h,i}[v_h]
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    w_h(x_i)-v_h(x_i)
  }\right)},
\]
which is \eqref{eq:canonical-source-supergradient}.
head: environment

label: lem:discrete-supergradient-representation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Finite-dimensional supergradient representation

label: eq:permutation-source
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathfrak S_h$ be the set of permutations of $\mathcal N_h$. For
$\pi\in\mathfrak S_h$, define $r_{\pi,0}:=0$ and
$r_{\pi,k}:=\sum_{\ell=1}^k\omega_{\pi(\ell)}$
and
\begin{equation}
  q_{\pi,\pi(k)}
  :=
  \frac{1}{\omega_{\pi(k)}}
  \int_{r_{\pi,k-1}}^{r_{\pi,k}}
  G(\rho) \ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\rho.
  \label{eq:permutation-source}
\end{equation}
With $L_\pi(w_h):=\sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}\omega_iq_{\pi,i}w_h(x_i)$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-rearrangement-representation} gives
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R_h(w_h)
  =
  \min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_h}
  L_\pi(w_h).
  \label{eq:finite-permutation-representation}
\end{equation}
If $\mathfrak S_h(v_h):=\ensuremath{\left\{{\pi:L_\pi(v_h)=\mathcal R_h(v_h)}\right\}}$,
then the superdifferential of $\mathcal R_h$ at $v_h$ is
\begin{equation}
  \partial^+\mathcal R_h(v_h)
  =
  \operatorname{co}
  \ensuremath{\left\{{
    L_\pi:
    \pi\in\mathfrak S_h(v_h)
  }\right\}},
  \label{eq:finite-superdifferential}
\end{equation}
where $\operatorname{co}$ denotes the convex hull. Hence
$\ell_h=\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_h(v_h)}\lambda_\pi L_\pi$, where
$\lambda_\pi\geq0$ and $\sum_\pi\lambda_\pi=1$. The coefficients
$q_{h,i}:=\sum_{\pi}\lambda_\pi q_{\pi,i}$ satisfy
$0\leq q_{h,i}\leq M_\alpha$
and
\[
  \ell_h(w_h)
  =
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_{h,i}w_h(x_i)
  \qquad
  \text{for every }w_h\inV_h.
\]
Since $\ell_h$ is a supergradient at $v_h$, the vector $q_h$ therefore
satisfies
\eqref{eq:admissible-source-inequality} and is an admissible
rearrangement source.

Conversely, suppose that $q_h$ is an admissible rearrangement source
at $v_h$, and define
\[
  \ell_h(w_h)
  :=
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_{h,i}w_h(x_i).
\]
Then \eqref{eq:admissible-source-inequality} is precisely
\[
  \mathcal R_h(w_h)-\mathcal R_h(v_h)
  \leq
  \ell_h(w_h-v_h)
  \qquad
  \text{for every }w_h\inV_h.
\]
Hence $\ell_h\in\partial^+\mathcal R_h(v_h)$, completing the
equivalence.
head: environment

label: lem:discrete-energy-coercivity
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Coercivity of the discrete energy

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemmas~\ref{lem:discrete-rearrangement-concavity}
and~\ref{lem:lumped-norm-equivalence},
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|\mathcal R_h(v_h)\right|}
  \leq
  M_\alpha
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_i\ensuremath{\left|v_h(x_i)\right|}
  \leq
  C\ensuremath{\left\|v_h\right\|}_{L^2(\Omega_h)}.
\]
The Poincaré inequality for the zero extension to $\Omega$ gives
$\ensuremath{\left|\mathcal R_h(v_h)\right|}\leq C\ensuremath{\left\|\nabla v_h\right\|}_{L^2(\Omega_h)}$,
which proves the claim.
head: environment

label: lem:discrete-well-posedness
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Discrete existence, uniqueness and optimality

title: Proof
body_md:
The functional $-\mathcal R_h$ is convex and continuous, while
$v_h\longmapsto\frac12a_h(v_h,v_h)$ is strictly convex on $V_h$.
Hence $\mathcal J_h$ is strictly convex.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-energy-coercivity}, it is also coercive.
Since $V_h$ is finite dimensional, $\mathcal J_h$ therefore has a
unique minimiser.

We prove the equivalence in the order
$(1)\Longrightarrow(3)\Longrightarrow(2)\Longrightarrow(1)$.

Suppose first that $u_h$ minimises $\mathcal J_h$. The
finite-dimensional convex optimality condition gives a supergradient
$\ell_h\in\partial^+\mathcal R_h(u_h)$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
  a_h(u_h,v_h)
  =
  \ell_h(v_h)
  \qquad
  \text{for every }v_h\inV_h.
  \label{eq:technical-optimality-balance}
\end{equation}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-supergradient-representation}, there is an
admissible source $q_h^\ast$ at $u_h$ representing $\ell_h$. Hence
\[
  a_h(u_h,v_h)
  =
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_{h,i}^\ast v_h(x_i)
  \qquad
  \text{for every }v_h\inV_h,
\]
which proves $(1)\Rightarrow(3)$.

Now suppose that $(3)$ holds. Since $q_h^\ast$ is admissible at $u_h$,
\[
  \mathcal R_h(v_h)-\mathcal R_h(u_h)
  \leq
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_{h,i}^\ast
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    v_h(x_i)-u_h(x_i)
  }\right)}.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:technical-discrete-source-equation} with
$v_h-u_h$ therefore gives $\mathcal R_h(v_h)-\mathcal R_h(u_h)
\leq a_h(u_h,v_h-u_h)$,
which is \eqref{eq:technical-discrete-VI}. Thus
$(3)\Rightarrow(2)$.

Finally, suppose that $(2)$ holds. Expanding the quadratic term gives
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal J_h(v_h)-\mathcal J_h(u_h)
  &=
  a_h(u_h,v_h-u_h)
  +
  \frac12
  a_h(v_h-u_h,v_h-u_h)
  \\
  &\qquad
  -
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    \mathcal R_h(v_h)-\mathcal R_h(u_h)
  }\right)}.
\end{align*}
By \eqref{eq:technical-discrete-VI},
\[
  \mathcal J_h(v_h)-\mathcal J_h(u_h)
  \geq
  \frac12
  a_h(v_h-u_h,v_h-u_h)
  \geq
  0.
\]
Hence $u_h$ minimises $\mathcal J_h$, proving $(2)\Rightarrow(1)$.
The same inequality also recovers uniqueness from strict convexity.
head: environment

label: lem:discrete-barrier-bound
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Discrete barrier bound

title: Proof
body_md:
For $i\in\mathcal N_h^\circ$, $a_h(u_h,\varphi_i)=\omega_iq_{h,i}^\ast$,
where $0\leq q_{h,i}^\ast\leq M_\alpha$. Hence
$0\leq a_h(u_h,\varphi_i)\leq M_\alpha\omega_i=
a_h(z_h,\varphi_i)$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-comparison} applied twice gives
$0\lequ_h(x_i)\leq z_h(x_i)$ for every $i\in\mathcal N_h^\circ$.
head: environment

label: lem:rearrangement-iteration-invariance
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:rearrangement-iteration-invariance}
If $u_h^n\in K_h$, then
$\widehat u_h^{n+1}\in K_h$. Consequently, $u_h^0\in K_h$ implies
$u_h^n\in K_h$ for every $n\geq0$.
head: environment
name: Invariance of the rearrangement iteration

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $0\leq q_{h,i}^n\leq M_\alpha$,
$0\leq a_h(\widehat u_h^{n+1},\varphi_i)\leq
a_h(z_h,\varphi_i)$.
The comparison principle gives
$\widehat u_h^{n+1}\in K_h$. The set $K_h$ is convex, so the relaxed
update also belongs to $K_h$.
head: environment

label: lem:rearrangement-iteration-convergence
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Convergence of the rearrangement iteration

label: eq:iteration-subgradient-identity
title: Proof
body_md:
Write
\[
  \ensuremath{\left\|v_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2
  :=
  a_h(v_h,v_h),
  \qquad
  d_h^n
  :=
  u_h^n-\widehat u_h^{n+1}.
\]
The Poisson step gives
\begin{equation}
  a_h(d_h^n,v_h)
  =
  a_h(u_h^n,v_h)
  -
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_{h,i}^nv_h(x_i).
  \label{eq:iteration-subgradient-identity}
\end{equation}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-source-supergradient},
$q_h^n=\overline q_h[u_h^n]$ represents a supergradient of
$\mathcal R_h$ at $u_h^n$, and hence
\[
  \mathcal R_h(v_h)-\mathcal R_h(u_h^n)
  \leq
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_{h,i}^n
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    v_h(x_i)-u_h^n(x_i)
  }\right)}.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:iteration-subgradient-identity} with
$v_h-u_h^n$ in place of $v_h$ therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal J_h(v_h)-\mathcal J_h(u_h^n)
  &\geq
  \frac12
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    \ensuremath{\left\|v_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2
    -
    \ensuremath{\left\|u_h^n\right\|}_{a_h}^2
  }\right)}
  -
  a_h(
    u_h^n,
    v_h-u_h^n
  )
  +
  a_h(
    d_h^n,
    v_h-u_h^n
  )
  \\
  &=
  \frac12
  \ensuremath{\left\|v_h-u_h^n\right\|}_{a_h}^2
  +
  a_h(
    d_h^n,
    v_h-u_h^n
  ).
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal J_h(v_h)
  \geq
  \mathcal J_h(u_h^n)
  +
  a_h(d_h^n,v_h-u_h^n)
  +
  \frac12
  \ensuremath{\left\|v_h-u_h^n\right\|}_{a_h}^2.
  \label{eq:strong-subgradient-inequality}
\end{equation}

Taking $v_h=u_h$ and using the minimality
$\mathcal J_h(u_h)\leq\mathcal J_h(u_h^n)$ yields
\begin{equation}
  a_h(
    d_h^n,
    u_h^n-u_h
  )
  \geq
  \frac12
  \ensuremath{\left\|u_h^n-u_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2.
  \label{eq:subgradient-distance-control}
\end{equation}

Since
\[
  u_h^{n+1}
  =
  u_h^n-\theta_nd_h^n,
\]
we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \ensuremath{\left\|u_h^{n+1}-u_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2
  &=
  \ensuremath{\left\|
    u_h^n-u_h-\theta_nd_h^n
  \right\|}_{a_h}^2
  \\
  &=
  \ensuremath{\left\|u_h^n-u_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2
  -
  2\theta_n
  a_h(
    d_h^n,
    u_h^n-u_h
  )
  +
  \theta_n^2
  \ensuremath{\left\|d_h^n\right\|}_{a_h}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying \eqref{eq:subgradient-distance-control} to the middle term
gives
\[
  \ensuremath{\left\|u_h^{n+1}-u_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2
  \leq
  (1-\theta_n)
  \ensuremath{\left\|u_h^n-u_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2
  +
  \theta_n^2
  \ensuremath{\left\|d_h^n\right\|}_{a_h}^2.
\]

By Lemma~\ref{lem:rearrangement-iteration-invariance}, the two points
$u_h^n$ and $\widehat u_h^{n+1}$ remain in the compact set $K_h$.
Thus, for fixed $h$,
\[
  \ensuremath{\left\|d_h^n\right\|}_{a_h}
  =
  \ensuremath{\left\|
    u_h^n-\widehat u_h^{n+1}
  \right\|}_{a_h}
  \leq
  C_h.
\]
Setting $e_n:=\ensuremath{\left\|u_h^n-u_h\right\|}_{a_h}^2$ gives
\begin{equation}
  e_{n+1}
  \leq
  (1-\theta_n)e_n
  +
  C_h^2\theta_n^2.
  \label{eq:iteration-recursion}
\end{equation}
We now show directly that $e_n\to0$. Fix $N\geq0$. Iterating
\eqref{eq:iteration-recursion} gives
\begin{align}
  e_{n+1}
  &\leq
  e_N
  \prod_{k=N}^{n}
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    1-\theta_k
  }\right)}
  \nonumber\\
  &\quad
  +
  C_h^2
  \sum_{j=N}^{n}
  \theta_j^2
  \prod_{k=j+1}^{n}
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    1-\theta_k
  }\right)}.
  \label{eq:iteration-recursion-product}
\end{align}
Since $0<\theta_k\leq1$ and $\sum_k\theta_k=\infty$,
$\prod_{k=N}^{n}\ensuremath{\!\left({1-\theta_k}\right)}\longrightarrow0$ as $n\to\infty$.
Moreover, every product in the sum is bounded by one, so
$\limsup_{n\to\infty}e_n\leq C_h^2\sum_{j=N}^{\infty}\theta_j^2$.
Because $\sum_j\theta_j^2<\infty$, the right-hand side tends to zero
as $N\to\infty$. Hence $e_n\to0$, proving
\eqref{eq:technical-iteration-H1-convergence}.

The $L^\infty$ conclusion follows from equivalence of norms on the
fixed finite-dimensional space $V_h$.
head: environment

label: eq:certificate-supergradient-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0\leq j\leq n$. Since $q_h^j$ represents a supergradient of
$\mathcal R_h$ at $u_h^j$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R_h(v_h)
  -
  \mathcal R_h(u_h^j)
  \leq
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_h}
  \omega_iq_{h,i}^j
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    v_h(x_i)-u_h^j(x_i)
  }\right)}
  \label{eq:certificate-supergradient-bound}
\end{equation}
for every $v_h\inV_h$. By the defining Poisson equation for
$\widehat u_h^{j+1}$, the right-hand side equals
$a_h\ensuremath{\!\left({\widehat u_h^{j+1},v_h-u_h^j}\right)}$.
It follows that
\begin{align}
  \mathcal J_h(v_h)
  &=
  \frac12a_h(v_h,v_h)
  -
  \mathcal R_h(v_h)
  \nonumber\\
  &\geq
  \frac12a_h(v_h,v_h)
  -
  \mathcal R_h(u_h^j)
  -
  a_h\ensuremath{\!\left({
    \widehat u_h^{j+1},
    v_h-u_h^j
  }\right)}
  \nonumber\\
  &=
  \frac12
  a_h\ensuremath{\!\left({
    v_h-\widehat u_h^{j+1},
    v_h-\widehat u_h^{j+1}
  }\right)}
  +
  \ell_h^j.
  \label{eq:certificate-completed-square}
\end{align}
Hence $\mathcal J_h(v_h)\geq\ell_h^j$ for every $v_h\inV_h$.
Taking $v_h=u_h$ gives $\ell_h^j\leq\mathcal J_h^\star$. Since this
holds for every $0\leq j\leq n$,
$L_h^n=\max_{0\leq j\leq n}\ell_h^j\leq\mathcal J_h^\star$. On the
other hand, the minimality of $u_h$ gives
$\mathcal J_h^\star\leq\mathcal J_h(u_h^n)=\mathcal J_h^n$.
This proves
\eqref{eq:certified-energy-bracket}, and therefore
\[
  0
  \leq
  \mathcal J_h^n-\mathcal J_h^\star
  \leq
  \mathcal J_h^n-L_h^n
  =
  \eta_h^n,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:certified-energy-error}.

Finally, the strong convexity estimate from
Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-well-posedness} gives
\[
  \mathcal J_h(u_h^n)
  -
  \mathcal J_h(u_h)
  \geq
  \frac12
  a_h\ensuremath{\!\left({
    u_h^n-u_h,
    u_h^n-u_h
  }\right)}.
\]
Combining this inequality with
\eqref{eq:certified-energy-error} yields
\[
  \ensuremath{\left\|
    \nabla(u_h^n-u_h)
  \right\|}_{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname L}\xspace^{2}}(\Omega_h)}
  \leq
  \sqrt{2\eta_h^n},
\]
which is \eqref{eq:certified-energy-norm-error}.

label: lem:continuum-rearrangement-properties
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Continuum rearrangement functional

label: eq:continuum-minimum-representation
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $G$ is nondecreasing, the Hardy--Littlewood rearrangement
inequality and the characterisation of equimeasurable rearrangements
\cite{HardyLittlewoodPolya1952,Ryff1965},
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R(v)
  =
  \inf_{q\sim G}
  \int_\Omega vq\,\mathrm dx.
  \label{eq:continuum-minimum-representation}
\end{equation}
Indeed, among all spatial rearrangements of $G$, the integral is
minimised by pairing the decreasing rearrangement of $v$ with the
increasing rearrangement of $G$, which is $G$ itself.

For every fixed $q\sim G$, the map
\[
  v
  \longmapsto
  \int_\Omega
  vq\,\mathrm dx
\]
is linear. Hence \eqref{eq:continuum-minimum-representation} expresses
$\mathcal R$ as an infimum of linear functionals, and therefore
$\mathcal R$ is concave.

Equimeasurability preserves the essential range. Since
\[
  0
  \leq
  G
  \leq
  M_\alpha
  \qquad
  \text{almost everywhere on }(0,\ensuremath{\left|\Omega\right|}),
\]
every $q\sim G$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  0
  \leq
  q
  \leq
  M_\alpha
  \qquad
  \text{almost everywhere in }\Omega.
  \label{eq:continuum-rearranged-source-bound}
\end{equation}

Let $\varepsilon>0$ and choose $q_\varepsilon\sim G$ such that
\[
  \int_\Omega
  wq_\varepsilon\,\mathrm dx
  \leq
  \mathcal R(w)+\varepsilon.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:continuum-minimum-representation} for $v$ gives
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal R(v)-\mathcal R(w)
  &\leq
  \int_\Omega
  vq_\varepsilon\,\mathrm dx
  -
  \int_\Omega
  wq_\varepsilon\,\mathrm dx
  +
  \varepsilon
  \\
  &\leq
  M_\alpha
  \ensuremath{\left\|v-w\right\|}_{L^1(\Omega)}
  +
  \varepsilon.
\end{align*}
Letting $\varepsilon\to0$ and interchanging $v$ and $w$ proves
\eqref{eq:continuum-rearrangement-Lipschitz}.

Finally, $v\mapsto-\mathcal R(v)$ is convex, while
\[
  v
  \longmapsto
  \frac12
  \int_\Omega
  \ensuremath{\left|\nabla v\right|}^2\,\mathrm dx
\]
is strictly convex on $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega)$. Their sum $\mathcal J$ is
therefore strictly convex.

label: lem:continuum-no-secondary-plateaux
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Absence of non-maximal plateaux

label: eq:gradient-zero-on-level-set
title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
  E_t
  :=
  \ensuremath{\left\{{
    x\in\Omega:
    u(x)=t
  }\right\}}.
\]
Suppose that $\ensuremath{\left|E_t\right|}>0$. By the Stampacchia level-set property
\cite[Theorem~6.19]{Leoni2009},
\begin{equation}
  \nabla u
  =
  0
  \qquad
  \text{almost everywhere on }E_t.
  \label{eq:gradient-zero-on-level-set}
\end{equation}
Since $u\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname C}\xspace^{1,1}}(\overline\Omega)$, each first derivative
$\partial_j u$ belongs to $W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$. Moreover,
\eqref{eq:gradient-zero-on-level-set} gives
$\partial_j u=0$ almost everywhere on $E_t$. Applying the same
level-set property to $\partial_j u$ at level zero yields
\[
  \nabla(\partial_j u)
  =
  0
  \qquad
  \text{almost everywhere on }E_t.
\]
Since this holds for every $j$, we obtain
\[
  D^2u
  =
  0
  \qquad
  \text{almost everywhere on }E_t,
\]
and hence $\Delta u=0$ almost everywhere on $E_t$.

On the other hand, $t<M$ implies
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|u\geq t\right|}
  >
  \alpha.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:rank-law} therefore gives
\[
  -\Delta u
  =
  g\bigl(
    \ensuremath{\left|u\geq t\right|}
  \bigr)
  >
  0
  \qquad
  \text{almost everywhere on }E_t,
\]
which is a contradiction.
head: environment

label: lem:continuum-variational-characterisation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Continuum variational characterisation

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
  D_u
  :=
  \ensuremath{\left\{{
    x\in\Omega:
    u(x)=\max_{\overline\Omega}u
  }\right\}}.
\]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum-well-posedness},
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|D_u\right|}
  =
  \alpha.
\]
Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:continuum-no-secondary-plateaux} shows that
every level set below the maximum has zero measure.

Define the non-strict rank map
\[
  r_u(x)
  :=
  \ensuremath{\left|
    \ensuremath{\left\{{
      y\in\Omega:
      u(y)\geq u(x)
    }\right\}}
  \right|}.
\]
On the maximum plateau,
\begin{equation}
  r_u(x)
  =
  \alpha
  \qquad
  \text{for every }x\in D_u.
  \label{eq:continuum-plateau-rank}
\end{equation}
Away from $D_u$, the absence of positive-measure level sets implies
that the rank variable is uniformly distributed over
$(\alpha,\ensuremath{\left|\Omega\right|})$. More precisely, writing $\mathcal L^d$ for
$d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure, $\mu|_A$ for the restriction of a
measure $\mu$ to $A$, and $T_\#\mu$ for its pushforward under a map
$T$, we have
\begin{equation}
  (r_u)_\#
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    \mathcal L^2|_{\Omega\setminus D_u}
  }\right)}
  =
  \mathcal L^1|_{(\alpha,\ensuremath{\left|\Omega\right|})}.
  \label{eq:continuum-rank-pushforward}
\end{equation}
Indeed, let $s\in(\alpha,\ensuremath{\left|\Omega\right|})$. Since the level sets of $u$
below its maximum have zero measure, the distribution function
\[
  t
  \longmapsto
  \ensuremath{\left|u\geq t\right|}
\]
is continuous below the maximum. Hence there exists $t_s$ such that
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|u\geq t_s\right|}
  =
  s.
\]
Up to a null set,
\[
  \ensuremath{\left\{{
    x\in\Omega\setminus D_u:
    r_u(x)\leq s
  }\right\}}
  =
  \ensuremath{\left\{{
    x\in\Omega:
    u(x)\geq t_s
  }\right\}}
  \setminus D_u,
\]
and therefore
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|
    \ensuremath{\left\{{
      x\in\Omega\setminus D_u:
      r_u(x)\leq s
    }\right\}}
  \right|}
  =
  s-\alpha.
\]
This is precisely the distribution function of Lebesgue measure on
$(\alpha,\ensuremath{\left|\Omega\right|})$, and proves
\eqref{eq:continuum-rank-pushforward}.

Set
\begin{equation}
  q_u(x)
  :=
  G\ensuremath{\!\left({r_u(x)}\right)}.
\end{equation}
Since $G=0$ on $[0,\alpha]$, the plateau $D_u$ contributes mass
$\alpha$ at the value zero. Together with
\eqref{eq:continuum-rank-pushforward}, this shows that $q_u$ and $G$
have the same distribution of values. Thus
\begin{equation}
  q_u
  \sim
  G.
  \label{eq:continuum-source-equimeasurable}
\end{equation}

The functions $u$ and $q_u$ are oppositely ordered. Indeed, if
$u(x)>u(y)$, then
\[
  r_u(x)
  \leq
  r_u(y),
\]
and, since $G$ is nondecreasing,
\[
  q_u(x)
  \leq
  q_u(y).
\]
The opposite-order case of the Hardy--Littlewood rearrangement
inequality therefore gives
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R(u)
  =
  \int_\Omega
  uq_u\,\mathrm dx.
  \label{eq:continuum-source-attains-minimum}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, since $q_u\sim G$, the minimum representation
\eqref{eq:continuum-minimum-representation} gives
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R(v)
  \leq
  \int_\Omega
  vq_u\,\mathrm dx
  \qquad
  \text{for every }v\in L^1(\Omega).
  \label{eq:continuum-fixed-source-upper-bound}
\end{equation}
Subtracting \eqref{eq:continuum-source-attains-minimum} from
\eqref{eq:continuum-fixed-source-upper-bound} yields
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R(v)-\mathcal R(u)
  \leq
  \int_\Omega
  q_u(v-u)\,\mathrm dx,
\end{equation}
so $q_u$ is a supergradient of $\mathcal R$ at $u$.

Finally, $r_u(x)\geq\alpha$ throughout $\Omega$, and hence
\[
  q_u(x)
  =
  G\bigl(r_u(x)\bigr)
  =
  g\bigl(r_u(x)\bigr).
\]
The Grad--Mercier equation therefore gives
\[
  \int_\Omega
  \nabla u\cdot\nabla(v-u)\,\mathrm dx
  =
  \int_\Omega
  q_u(v-u)\,\mathrm dx
  \qquad
  \text{for every }v\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega).
\]
Using \eqref{eq:continuum-supergradient-inequality} and expanding the
quadratic term, we obtain
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal J(v)-\mathcal J(u)
  &=
  \int_\Omega
  \nabla u\cdot\nabla(v-u)\,\mathrm dx
  +
  \frac12
  \ensuremath{\left\|
    \nabla(v-u)
  \right\|}_{L^2(\Omega)}^2
  -
  \bigl(
    \mathcal R(v)-\mathcal R(u)
  \bigr)
  \\
  &\geq
  \frac12
  \ensuremath{\left\|
    \nabla(v-u)
  \right\|}_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.
\end{align*}
Thus $u$ minimises $\mathcal J$. The inequality is strict whenever
$v\neq u$, so $u$ is the unique minimiser.

label: lem:discrete-rearrangement-consistency
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Consistency of the weighted nodal rearrangement

label: eq:discrete-value-distribution-convergence
title: Proof
body_md:
Set
\[
  m_h
  :=
  \ensuremath{\left|\Omega_h\right|},
  \qquad
  m
  :=
  \ensuremath{\left|\Omega\right|},
\]
and define the distributions of the discrete and limiting functions by
\[
  \nu_h
  :=
  (\mathcal E_hv_h)_\#\mu_h,
  \qquad
  \nu
  :=
  v_\#
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    \mathcal L^2|_\Omega
  }\right)}.
\]
We first show that
\begin{equation}
  \nu_h
  \rightharpoonup
  \nu
  \qquad
  \text{weakly as finite measures on }\mathbb R.
  \label{eq:discrete-value-distribution-convergence}
\end{equation}
Indeed, let $\eta\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname C}\xspace^{0}}(\mathbb R)$. The functions
$\mathcal E_hv_h$ and $v$ are uniformly bounded for sufficiently small
$h$, so only the restriction of $\eta$ to a fixed compact interval is
relevant. By \eqref{eq:uniform-function-convergence},
\[
  \eta(\mathcal E_hv_h)
  \longrightarrow
  \eta(v)
  \qquad
  \text{uniformly on }\overline\Omega.
\]
Consequently, Lemma~\ref{lem:nodal-measure-convergence} gives
\begin{align*}
  \int_{\mathbb R}
  \eta(t)\ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\nu_h(t)
  &=
  \int_{\overline\Omega}
  \eta(\mathcal E_hv_h)
  \ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\mu_h
  \\
  &\longrightarrow
  \int_\Omega
  \eta(v)\,\mathrm dx
  =
  \int_{\mathbb R}
  \eta(t)\ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}}\nu(t),
\end{align*}
which proves \eqref{eq:discrete-value-distribution-convergence}.

Choose $B>0$ such that
\[
  \ensuremath{\left|\mathcal E_hv_h\right|}
  \leq
  B,
  \qquad
  \ensuremath{\left|v\right|}
  \leq
  B
\]
for all sufficiently small $h$, and set
\[
  c_0
  :=
  -B-1.
\]
Since $\Omega_h\subset\Omega$, we have $m_h\leq m$. Define the augmented
measure
\begin{equation}
  \widehat\nu_h
  :=
  \nu_h
  +
  (m-m_h)\delta_{c_0}.
  \label{eq:augmented-pushforward-measure}
\end{equation}
The measures $\widehat\nu_h$ and $\nu$ have the same total mass $m$,
are supported in a common compact interval, and satisfy
\[
  \widehat\nu_h
  \rightharpoonup
  \nu.
\]
Weak convergence on a common compact support implies convergence in the
one-dimensional Wasserstein distance $W_1$. Equivalently, the decreasing
quantiles converge in $L^1(0,m)$.

Let $\widehat v_h^\ast$ denote the decreasing quantile of
$\widehat\nu_h$. Since $c_0$ lies strictly below the values of
$\mathcal E_hv_h$, the added mass occupies the final part of the rank
interval, and hence
\[
  \widehat v_h^\ast(r)
  =
  \begin{cases}
    v_h^\ast(r),
      &0<r<m_h,
    \\
    c_0,
      &m_h<r<m.
  \end{cases}
\]
Therefore
\[
  \int_0^m
  \ensuremath{\left|
    \widehat v_h^\ast(r)-v^\ast(r)
  \right|}
  \ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}} r
  \longrightarrow0,
\]
and in particular
\begin{equation}
  \int_0^{m_h}
  \ensuremath{\left|
    v_h^\ast(r)-v^\ast(r)
  \right|}
  \ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}} r
  \longrightarrow0.
  \label{eq:augmented-quantile-convergence}
\end{equation}

By the definitions of the discrete and continuum rearrangement
functionals,
\[
  \mathcal R_h(v_h)
  =
  \int_0^{m_h}
  G(r)v_h^\ast(r)\ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}} r,
  \qquad
  \mathcal R(v)
  =
  \int_0^m
  G(r)v^\ast(r)\ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}} r.
\]
Since $0\leq G\leq M_\alpha$ and $\ensuremath{\left|v^\ast\right|}\leq B$,
\begin{align*}
  \ensuremath{\left|
    \mathcal R_h(v_h)-\mathcal R(v)
  \right|}
  &\leq
  M_\alpha
  \int_0^{m_h}
  \ensuremath{\left|
    v_h^\ast(r)-v^\ast(r)
  \right|}
  \ensuremath{\,\mathrm{d}} r
  \\
  &\quad
  +
  M_\alpha B
  (m-m_h).
\end{align*}
The first term tends to zero by
\eqref{eq:augmented-quantile-convergence}, while the second tends to
zero because $\ensuremath{\left|\Omega_h\right|}\to\ensuremath{\left|\Omega\right|}$. This proves
\eqref{eq:rearrangement-functional-convergence}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Existence, uniqueness and the inclusion
\[
  u_h\in K_h
\]
follow from Lemmas~\ref{lem:discrete-well-posedness}
and~\ref{lem:discrete-barrier-bound}. For each fixed $h$, convergence of
the rearrangement iteration to $u_h$ follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:rearrangement-iteration-convergence}.

We now consider the limit $h\to0$. Let $h_k\to0$ be arbitrary. For each
$k$, choose any admissible equilibrium source
\[
  q_{h_k}^\ast
  =
  \ensuremath{\!\left({
    q_{h_k,i}^\ast
  }\right)}_{i\in\mathcal N_{h_k}}
\]
satisfying \eqref{eq:discrete-source-equation}, and define
\[
  s_{h_k}^\ast
  :=
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_{h_k}}
  q_{h_k,i}^\ast\varphi_i.
\]
The admissible source bounds imply
\[
  0
  \leq
  s_{h_k}^\ast
  \leq
  M_\alpha
  \qquad
  \text{in }\Omega_{h_k}.
\]
Hence there exist a subsequence, not relabelled, and
$f\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname L}\xspace^{\infty}}(\Omega)$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \widetilde{s_{h_k}^\ast}
  \stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}
  f
  \qquad
  \text{in }\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname L}\xspace^{\infty}}(\Omega)
  \quad\text{as }k\to\infty.
  \label{eq:technical-source-subsequence}
\end{equation}

The discrete equilibrium equation is a mass-lumped Poisson problem.
Lemma~\ref{lem:linear-compactness-consistency} therefore gives a
function $w\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega)$ such that
\begin{align}
  \mathcal E_{h_k}u_{h_k}
  &\longrightarrow
  w
  &&\text{strongly in }\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega),
  \label{eq:technical-subsequence-H1}
  \\
  \mathcal E_{h_k}u_{h_k}
  &\longrightarrow
  w
  &&\text{strongly in }\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname L}\xspace^{\infty}}(\Omega),
  \label{eq:technical-subsequence-Linf}
\end{align}
and
\begin{equation}
  \int_\Omega
  \nabla w\cdot\nabla\phi\,\mathrm dx
  =
  \int_\Omega
  f\phi\,\mathrm dx
  \qquad
  \text{for every }\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega).
  \label{eq:technical-limit-Poisson}
\end{equation}

Let $\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname C}\xspace^{\infty}}_c(\Omega)$ and set
\[
  \phi_{h_k}
  :=
  I_{h_k}\phi.
\]
For sufficiently large $k$, the support of $\phi$ lies inside
$\Omega_{h_k}$. Since $q_{h_k}^\ast$ is an admissible supergradient at
$u_{h_k}$,
\begin{align}
  \mathcal R_{h_k}(\phi_{h_k})
  -
  \mathcal R_{h_k}(u_{h_k})
  &\leq
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_{h_k}}
  \omega_iq_{h_k,i}^\ast
  \bigl(
    \phi_{h_k}(x_i)-u_{h_k}(x_i)
  \bigr)
  \nonumber\\
  &=
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_{h_k}}
  \omega_iq_{h_k,i}^\ast
  \phi_{h_k}(x_i)
  -
  a_{h_k}(u_{h_k},u_{h_k}).
  \label{eq:technical-pass-supergradient}
\end{align}

Lemma~\ref{lem:mass-lumping-error} gives
\[
  \sum_{i\in\mathcal N_{h_k}}
  \omega_iq_{h_k,i}^\ast
  \phi_{h_k}(x_i)
  -
  \int_{\Omega_{h_k}}
  s_{h_k}^\ast\phi_{h_k}\,\mathrm dx
  \longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \mathcal E_{h_k}\phi_{h_k}
  \longrightarrow
  \phi
  \qquad
  \text{uniformly on }\overline\Omega.
\]
Together with
\eqref{eq:technical-source-subsequence}, this gives
\begin{equation}
  \int_{\Omega_{h_k}}
  s_{h_k}^\ast\phi_{h_k}\,\mathrm dx
  \longrightarrow
  \int_\Omega
  f\phi\,\mathrm dx.
  \label{eq:technical-source-test-limit}
\end{equation}

The strong $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega)$ convergence in
\eqref{eq:technical-subsequence-H1} gives
\[
  a_{h_k}(u_{h_k},u_{h_k})
  =
  \ensuremath{\left\|
    \nabla\mathcal E_{h_k}u_{h_k}
  \right\|}_{L^2(\Omega)}^2
  \longrightarrow
  \ensuremath{\left\|\nabla w\right\|}_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.
\]
Testing \eqref{eq:technical-limit-Poisson} with $\phi=w$ then yields
\begin{equation}
  a_{h_k}(u_{h_k},u_{h_k})
  \longrightarrow
  \int_\Omega
  fw\,\mathrm dx.
  \label{eq:technical-discrete-energy-limit}
\end{equation}

Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete-rearrangement-consistency}, applied to
\eqref{eq:technical-subsequence-Linf} and to the interpolants
$\phi_{h_k}$, gives
\begin{align}
  \mathcal R_{h_k}(u_{h_k})
  &\longrightarrow
  \mathcal R(w),
  \label{eq:technical-solution-rearrangement-limit}
  \\
  \mathcal R_{h_k}(\phi_{h_k})
  &\longrightarrow
  \mathcal R(\phi).
  \label{eq:technical-test-rearrangement-limit}
\end{align}
Passing to the limit in
\eqref{eq:technical-pass-supergradient} therefore yields
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R(\phi)-\mathcal R(w)
  \leq
  \int_\Omega
  f(\phi-w)\,\mathrm dx
  \qquad
  \text{for every }\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname C}\xspace^{\infty}}_c(\Omega).
  \label{eq:technical-limit-supergradient}
\end{equation}

Since $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname C}\xspace^{\infty}}_c(\Omega)$ is dense in $L^1(\Omega)$,
$f\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname L}\xspace^{\infty}}(\Omega)$, and $\mathcal R$ is Lipschitz continuous on
$L^1(\Omega)$, the inequality extends to
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal R(\phi)-\mathcal R(w)
  \leq
  \int_\Omega
  f(\phi-w)\,\mathrm dx
  \qquad
  \text{for every }\phi\in L^1(\Omega).
  \label{eq:technical-limit-supergradient-L1}
\end{equation}

For $\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega)$,
\eqref{eq:technical-limit-Poisson} gives
\[
  \int_\Omega
  \nabla w\cdot\nabla(\phi-w)\,\mathrm dx
  =
  \int_\Omega
  f(\phi-w)\,\mathrm dx.
\]
Combining this identity with
\eqref{eq:technical-limit-supergradient-L1} yields
\[
  \int_\Omega
  \nabla w\cdot\nabla(\phi-w)\,\mathrm dx
  \geq
  \mathcal R(\phi)-\mathcal R(w)
  \qquad
  \text{for every }\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega).
\]
Thus $w$ minimises the continuum energy $\mathcal J$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:continuum-variational-characterisation}, the unique
minimiser is the continuum Grad--Mercier solution, and therefore
\begin{equation}
  w
  =
  u.
  \label{eq:technical-subsequence-identification}
\end{equation}

It remains to identify the weak-star limit of the reconstructed sources.
Substituting $w=u$ into \eqref{eq:technical-limit-Poisson} gives
\begin{equation}
  \int_\Omega
  \nabla u\cdot\nabla\phi\,\mathrm dx
  =
  \int_\Omega
  f\phi\,\mathrm dx
  \qquad
  \text{for every }\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega).
  \label{eq:technical-limit-source-equation}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, the weak formulation of the continuum
Grad--Mercier equation gives
\begin{equation}
  \int_\Omega
  \nabla u\cdot\nabla\phi\,\mathrm dx
  =
  \int_\Omega
  g\bigl(
    \ensuremath{\left|u\geq u(\cdot)\right|}
  \bigr)
  \phi\,\mathrm dx
  \qquad
  \text{for every }\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega).
  \label{eq:technical-continuum-source-equation}
\end{equation}
Subtracting
\eqref{eq:technical-continuum-source-equation} from
\eqref{eq:technical-limit-source-equation} gives
\[
  \int_\Omega
  \ensuremath{\!\left[{
    f
    -
    g\ensuremath{\!\left({
      \ensuremath{\left|u\geq u(\cdot)\right|}
    }\right)}
  }\right]}
  \phi\,\mathrm dx
  =
  0
  \qquad
  \text{for every }\phi\in \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname C}\xspace^{\infty}}_c(\Omega).
\]
Therefore
\begin{equation}
  f
  =
  g\ensuremath{\!\left({
    \ensuremath{\left|u\geq u(\cdot)\right|}
  }\right)}
  \qquad
  \text{almost everywhere in }\Omega.
  \label{eq:technical-source-identification}
\end{equation}

The sequence $h_k\to0$ was arbitrary, and every convergent subsequence
has the same limit $u$. The subsequence principle therefore gives
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal E_hu_h
  &\longrightarrow
  u
  &&\text{strongly in }\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname H}\xspace}^{1}_0(\Omega),
  \\
  \mathcal E_hu_h
  &\longrightarrow
  u
  &&\text{strongly in }\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname L}\xspace^{\infty}}(\Omega)
\end{align*}
as $h\to0$.

The admissible equilibrium sources were also chosen arbitrarily. Every
weak-star accumulation point of their reconstructions is identified by
\eqref{eq:technical-source-identification}. Consequently, for every
choice of admissible equilibrium sources $q_h^\ast$,
\[
  \widetilde{s_h^\ast}
  \stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}
  g\ensuremath{\!\left({
    \ensuremath{\left|u\geq u(\cdot)\right|}
  }\right)}
  \qquad
  \text{in }\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\operatorname L}\xspace^{\infty}}(\Omega)
  \quad\text{as }h\to0.
\]

Finally, the maximum plateau has measure $\alpha$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum-well-posedness}, and the absence of
positive-measure level sets below the maximum follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:continuum-no-secondary-plateaux}.
